_comment: Field battles: an army holding a hex fights any horde whose route crosses it. Ambush: on `ambush.terrain`, with the army in place `ambush.prepMinutes` game minutes before the horde arrives, the defenders' first round hits `ambush.bonus` harder and the horde fights it without its stance. Choke point: a passable hex with at least `choke.minBlockedNeighbors` impassable neighbours; attackers hit `choke.attackerFactor` as hard there, and Hold the Line gains `choke.holdTheLineDefense` defense. River: a horde that crossed a river into the hex it fights in (over a bridge; nothing crosses elsewhere) hits `river.attackerFactor` as hard, at walls or in the field. Forts are built within `fort.range` hexes of a village and give armies holding them `fort.defenseBonus` defense; each keeps up to `fort.grainCapacity` grain. Supply points are built like forts (within `supplyPoint.range` hexes, paid from the village, standing after `supplyPoint.buildSeconds`) and keep up to `supplyPoint.grainCapacity` grain, but give no defense. An army that arrives at or stands on a fort or supply point fills up from its grain as it would in a village, and a standing army can leave grain there from its own supply. A horde that passes within its raid reach of a supply point (built or being built) burns it, grain and all, unless an army stands on it; forts keep their grain behind their walls. Bridges are built over a river edge within `bridge.range` hexes of a village (game seconds, divided by world speed); until one stands nothing crosses there, hordes included. Roads are built between two neighbouring hexes within `road.range` of a village, and improved twice more: each of `road.levels` is paid from the village and done after its `buildSeconds`, and moving along a road costs its level's `factor` of the terrain (a road being improved keeps its level until the work is done), for players and the human hordes alike, but the Monsters of the North keep off them. Wagon fort: an army holding open ground (no fort, supply point or village) with wagons (units.json `wagon`) can draw them into a ring, ready after `wagonFort.setupMinutes` game minutes; it gives `wagonFort.bonusPerWagon` defense for each wagon per `wagonFort.menPerWagon` soldiers (wagons x bonusPerWagon / ceil(soldiers / menPerWagon)), at most `wagonFort.maxBonus`, and breaks up when the army moves.
